definition: A structured process in which an AI agent breaks a task into steps, uses tools, and iterates based on intermediate results, rather than producing a single-shot response.
details: Agentic workflows often include planning, tool use, self-critique, and iterative refinement, extending simple prompting into more autonomous, multi-step problem solving.
story: Think of a chess player who never commits to a move blindly — they consider the board, try an action, watch what changes, and only then decide what is next. In plain words: A structured process in which an AI agent breaks a task into steps, uses tools, and iterates based on intermediate results, rather than producing a single-shot response. Here is how it actually plays out: Agentic workflows often include planning, tool use, self-critique, and iterative refinement, extending simple prompting into more autonomous, multi-step problem solving. The model stops being a one-shot answer machine and becomes a coworker that checks its own work. That loop of reason, act, and observe is Agentic Workflow.
